plan.name: Marathon Training: Intermediate 2
plan.author: Hal Higdon
plan.description: This is Intermediate 2. The Novice 1 and Advanced 2 training programs in my Marathon Training Guide represent the extremes. The former programs are designed for runners running their first marathons, or experienced runners who are happy with that level of training and see no need to do more. cross_training.label: Cross Training
cross_training.description: A non-running aerobic session used to maintain fitness while reducing running impact.

easy_run.label: Easy Run
easy_run.description: An easy aerobic run done at a comfortable, conversational pace to build endurance while limiting fatigue.

long_run.label: Long Run
long_run.description: The key to the program is the long run on weekends, which builds from 10 miles in the first week to a maximum of 20 miles. Although some experienced runners do train longer, I see no advantage in doing 23, 26 or even 31 mile runs. (I've tried that myself in the past, and it just wore me out.) Save your energy and concentrate on quality runs the rest of the week. Consistency is most important. You can skip an occasional workout, or juggle the schedule depending on other commitments, but do not cheat on the long runs. Notice that although the weekly long runs get progressively longer, every third week is a "stepback" week, where we reduce mileage to allow you to gather strength for the next push upward. Rest is an important component of any training program.

pace_run.label: Pace Run
pace_run.description: A run done at planned race pace to practice rhythm, pacing control, and race-specific effort.

race.label: Race
race.description: A race effort or tune-up event used to practice pacing and measure current fitness.

rest.label: Rest
rest.description: A no-training day used to absorb prior workouts and promote recovery.
